advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Exclude the run-scoped step from `required_steps` in `_equivalent_close_at` so cross-run equivalent closes are recognized (match the run_id-agnostic identity used by `_matches_basis`).
evidence: completion_bundle.py signature check: `required_steps.issubset(set(manifest))` — winner's manifest carries the winner's own run_id, not the loser's
docs/concurrency.md: 'a loser can recognize the equivalent signed close'
advisory.finding: `_equivalent_close_at` builds `required_steps` from `_basis_steps(basis)`, which includes the run-scoped step `completion-run:<basis.run_id>`, and then requires `required_steps.issubset(set(manifest))` of the WINNING close's signed manifest. Two independent completion runs racing on the same ticket have different `run_id`s, so the winner's manifest will not contain the loser's run_id step and equivalence is never recognized for a genuine cross-run race — the exact scenario the docstring ('Recognize the same certified basis after a same-ticket local or remote race') and the concurrency docs ('a loser can recognize the equivalent signed close') promise. The loser instead raises an exit-10 conflict. This also makes the two equivalence halves inconsistent: `_matches_basis` (sidecar check) deliberately compares only code_oid/tickets_oid/receipt_digest and ignores run_id.
scenarios: Two agents/processes each run completion verification for the same ticket at the same code+tickets OID; one wins the atomic close, the loser revalidates, finds the tracker advanced, and calls `_equivalent_close_at` — the signed-close half rejects because the winner's manifest run_id != loser's run_id.
advisory.suggested_fix: Compute `required_steps` from the run-independent identity (code_oid, tickets_oid, receipt_digest) rather than `_basis_steps` which includes `completion-run:<run_id>`; keep run_id only for the current run's own manifest, not for equivalence subset matching.
